title: Diversity of Life
tagline: Classification, the origin of life, bacteria and archaea, protists, fungi, land plants, invertebrates and vertebrates
summary: About two million living species have been named, and many more await discovery. This course surveys the tree of life: how organisms are classified, how life began, and the major lineages — bacteria and archaea, protists, fungi, land plants, invertebrates and vertebrates — with their body plans, life cycles and evolutionary history.

chapters.title: Classifying life
chapters.summary: Taxonomy and systematics, binomial names, ranks and clades, and the three domains of life.

chapters.title: The origin and early history of life
chapters.summary: Prebiotic chemistry, the RNA world, the first cells and the oldest evidence of life.

chapters.title: Bacteria and archaea
chapters.summary: The structure, metabolic range and major lineages of the prokaryotes.

chapters.title: Protists and the origin of eukaryotes
chapters.summary: Endosymbiosis, the major eukaryotic supergroups, algae and protozoa.

chapters.title: Fungi
chapters.summary: Fungal structure, nutrition and life cycles, and lichens and mycorrhizae.

chapters.title: Land plants
chapters.summary: The move onto land, alternation of generations, and bryophytes, ferns, gymnosperms and flowering plants.

chapters.title: Invertebrate animals
chapters.summary: Animal body plans from sponges to arthropods and echinoderms, and the Cambrian explosion.

chapters.title: Chordates and vertebrates
chapters.summary: Fishes, the move onto land, amniotes, birds and mammals.
